info.name: OAN DA Broadcast
info.description:
Send a Broadcast message to Development Agents, and read it from the DA's side.

Base path: /api/v1/da-services

Route: POST /notifications/broadcast (Communications Officer or Admin). A broadcast becomes one notification for every DA with an active Development Agent grant inside the scope.

## Run order
1. Login as a Communications Officer or Admin (0. Sign in)
2. Send a broadcast (1. Send a broadcast)
3. Requests that are refused (2. Refused requests)
4. Login as a DA inside the scope, then read the notification (3. DA side)

## Scope rule
- Admin may target anything.
- A Communications Officer with no Region / Zone / Woreda on their grant is the national desk and may target anything.
- A Communications Officer with a scoped grant may only target inside that scope; scope=all is refused with 403.

## Auth
Bearer {{access_token}}. These routes are DA Services DocTypes and call no registry, so the local Login token works. SSO login works too and is what a deployed server uses; the collection then also sends X-CSRF-Token.

Saved responses are written from the API contract (da_services/api/v1/notifications.py), not captured live. Tokens, usr and pwd stay empty in the committed environment.

item.name: 0. Sign in
item.description: Sign in as a Communications Officer or Admin to send, and as a Development Agent to read. Login is the local DA Services login; SSO login is the Keycloak login a deployed server uses.

request.description: Local DA Services login. Stores access_token and refresh_token. Field names are usr and pwd. Set usr and pwd in the environment.

Keycloak login through OAN IAM in one call. Stores access_token and csrf_token; the collection then sends both on every request. Set usr, pwd and sso_key in the environment (sso_key is the login key of the user's role, for example agent). Use this on a deployed server, or whenever a route calls a registry.
Refresh access_token using refresh_token (local Login only).
Role, role label, menu paths and scope of the signed-in user. Check the role is Communications Officer or Admin before sending.

exec: pm.test("Who am I returns 200", function () { pm.response.to.have.status(200); });

item.name: 1. Send a broadcast
item.description:
Body: title (required, 140 characters or fewer), body, href (a portal path such as /notifications), scope (all, region, zone or woreda; default all), scope_value (required unless scope is all) and client_op_id (optional idempotency key).

Returns broadcast_id, scope, scope_value, recipients and duplicate. Every send is recorded as a DA Broadcast row and a DA Audit Event.

request.description: scope=all reaches every DA with an active grant. Allowed for Admin and for a Communications Officer with no Region / Zone / Woreda on their grant.

exec: pm.test("Send to all DAs returns 200", function () { pm.response.to.have.status(200); });

request.description: Reaches the DAs whose grant has this Region code.

exec: pm.test("Send to a Region returns 200", function () { pm.response.to.have.status(200); });

request.description: Reaches the DAs whose grant has this Zone code.

exec: pm.test("Send to a Zone returns 200", function () { pm.response.to.have.status(200); });

request.description: Reaches the DAs whose grant has this Woreda code.

body.raw:
{
  "title": "Seed distribution at the Woreda store",
  "body": "Open 08:00 to 16:00 this week.",
  "href": "/notifications",
  "scope": "woreda",
  "scope_value": "{{woreda}}"
}

exec: pm.test("Send to a Woreda returns 200", function () { pm.response.to.have.status(200); });

body.raw:
{
  "title": "Seed distribution at the Woreda store",
  "body": "Open 08:00 to 16:00 this week.",
  "href": "/notifications",
  "scope": "woreda",
  "scope_value": "{{woreda}}"
}

request.description: A new client_op_id is generated before the request and stored. The broadcast_id in the response is that client_op_id.

exec: pm.test("Send with client_op_id returns 200", function () { pm.response.to.have.status(200); });

item.name: Send again with the same client_op_id

request.description: Run after 'Send with client_op_id'. The original broadcast is returned with duplicate=true and nobody is notified twice.

exec: pm.test("Send again with the same client_op_id returns 200", function () { pm.response.to.have.status(200); });

item.name: 2. Refused requests
item.description: Each request is refused before anything is saved or sent.

request.description: title is required.
title must be 140 characters or fewer.

exec: pm.test("Title longer than 140 characters returns 400", function () { pm.response.to.have.status(400); });

request.description: scope must be one of all, region, zone, woreda.
scope_value is required for scope region, zone and woreda.

exec: pm.test("Scope without scope_value returns 400", function () { pm.response.to.have.status(400); });

request.description: href must be a portal path starting with '/', never an external URL.
No active Development Agent is assigned to the scope value, so nothing is sent and no DA Broadcast row is kept.

exec: pm.test("Scope with no DA returns 400", function () { pm.response.to.have.status(400); });

request.description: Sign in as a Development Agent (or any role other than Communications Officer and Admin) and send: refused with 403 and recorded as a denied DA Audit Event.

exec: pm.test("Signed in as a DA returns 403", function () { pm.response.to.have.status(403); });

item.name: 3. DA side: read the broadcast
item.description: Sign in as a DA inside the scope that was targeted. A user only ever sees and changes their own notifications.

request.description: The signed-in user's notifications, newest first. A broadcast has kind Broadcast. Stores the first notification's id as notification_id. meta carries unread_count, limit and start.

response.name: Notifications
response.body:
{
  "status": "success",
  "message": "Success",
  "data": [
    {
      "id": "NOTIFICATION_ID",
      "kind": "Broadcast",
      "title": "Fertiliser distribution starts Monday",
      "body": "Collect vouchers at the Woreda office.",
      "href": "/notifications",
      "read": false,
      "read_at": null,
      "event": "broadcast:BROADCAST_ID",
      "reference_doctype": null,
      "reference_name": null,
      "at": "2026-11-13T10:15:00"
    }
  ],
  "meta": {
    "api_version": "v1",
    "unread_count": 1,
    "limit": 20,
    "start": 0
  }
}

request.description: Only the notifications not read yet.

exec: pm.test("My unread notifications returns 200", function () { pm.response.to.have.status(200); });

request.description: Marks the notification read and returns it. Another user's notification is refused with 403.

exec: pm.test("Mark one notification read returns 200", function () { pm.response.to.have.status(200); });

response.name: Marked read

request.description: Marks every unread notification of the signed-in user read. Returns how many were updated.

exec: pm.test("Mark all notifications read returns 200", function () { pm.response.to.have.status(200); });
